claims.claim: An observational study of US adults ages 18 to 65 with type 2 diabetes linked starting GLP-1 drugs to about three to four additional cases of ischemic optic neuropathy per 10,000 patients over 18 months.
claims.episode_span: starting a GLP-1 receptor agonist was associated with a small rise in ischemic optic neuropathy
claims.source_title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
claims.supporting_quote: The increase in risk was small -- approximately three to four additional cases per 10,000 patients treated with GLP-1s over 18 months, but clinicians and patients should be aware of this potential association.

claims.claim: The GLP-1 vision study was published in Annals of Internal Medicine and led by Rutgers researchers including Chintan Dave.
claims.episode_span: Rutgers researchers, writing in Annals of Internal Medicine
claims.source_title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
claims.supporting_quote: The study, published in Annals of Internal Medicine , analyzed information from a large database of US adults ages 18 to 65 with Type 2 diabetes.

claims.claim: The authors said the association does not prove a direct causal effect of GLP-1 drugs on the optic nerve.
claims.episode_span: The authors said the association does not prove a direct causal effect
claims.source_title: US study links GLP-1 drugs to rare vision loss — ScienceDaily
claims.supporting_quote: The authors stressed that the identified association does not prove a direct causal effect of GLP-1 drugs on the optic nerve: differences in patients' accompanying health conditions may have affected the results.

claims.claim: More than 80 percent of ischemic optic neuropathy cases cited in the report are the nonarteritic anterior form, and cases were recorded more often among men and people ages 50 to 65.
claims.episode_span: More than 80 percent of ischemic optic neuropathy cases, on estimates cited by UA.NEWS, are the nonarteritic anterior form
claims.source_title: US study links GLP-1 drugs to rare vision loss — ScienceDaily
claims.supporting_quote: More than 80% of cases, according to estimates cited in the article, involve the nonarteritic anterior form of the disease, in which the blood supply to the front part of the optic nerve is disrupted.

claims.source_title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
claims.supporting_quote: These medications include semaglutide (sold as Ozempic and Wegovy) and tirzepatide (sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound).

claims.claim: BPC-157 is a 15-amino-acid partial sequence of a body protection compound isolated from human gastric juice, and in rat tendon-fibroblast experiments it increased outgrowth, stress survival, and migration via FAK and paxillin phosphorylation without directly increasing proliferation.
claims.episode_span: BPC-157 is a pentadecapeptide of 15 amino acids, a partial sequence of a body-protection compound discovered in and isolated from human gastric juice.
claims.source_title: The promoting effect of pentadecapeptide BPC 157 on tendon healing involves tendon outgrowth, cell survival, and cell migration
claims.supporting_quote: Pentadecapeptide BPC 157, composed of 15 amino acids, is a partial sequence of body protection compound (BPC) that is discovered in and isolated from human gastric juice.

claims.claim: In rat gastric mucosa homogenates, BPC-157 induced nitric oxide generation that L-NAME did not inhibit as it inhibited L-arginine, and the peptide altered gastric-lesion and blood-pressure responses to L-NAME and L-arginine.
claims.episode_span: BPC-157 induced nitric-oxide generation comparable to L-arginine, and that L-NAME, which blocks nitric-oxide synthase, did not inhibit that peptide effect
claims.source_title: The influence of a novel pentadecapeptide, BPC 157, on N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methylester and L-arginine effects on stomach mucosa integrity and blood pressure
claims.supporting_quote: But, BPC 157 effect could not be inhibited by L-NAME, even when L-NAME was given in a tenfold (100 versus 1000 microM) higher dose than that needed for inhibition of the L-arginine effect.

claims.claim: A 2014 review says clinical translation of BPC-157 nitric-oxide modulation remains to be determined.
claims.episode_span: translating nitric-oxide modulation into better clinical performance “remains to be determined.”
claims.supporting_quote: However, how this advantage of modulating NO-system (i. e., particular effect on eNOS gene), may be practically translated into an enhanced clinical performance remains to be determined.

claims.claim: A 2013 review states BPC-157 was shown safe in inflammatory bowel disease clinical trials coded PL-10, PLD-116, and PL 14736, and that an LD1 was not achieved.
claims.episode_span: proven in clinical trials to be both safe in inflammatory bowel disease” under the codes PL-10, PLD-116, and PL 14736
claims.source_title: Toxicity by NSAIDs. Counteraction by stable gastric pentadecapeptide BPC 157
claims.supporting_quote: Stable gastric pentadecapeptide BPC 157 is an anti-ulcer peptidergic agent, proven in clinical trials to be both safe in inflammatory bowel disease (PL-10, PLD-116, PL 14736) and wound healing, stable in human gastric juice, with no toxicity being reported.

claims.claim: A 2026 critical review of rodent ischemia-reperfusion studies associated BPC-157 with less oxidative injury and VEGF-related signaling changes but did not perform a meta-analysis because the studies were heterogeneous.
claims.episode_span: The reviewers did not pool the studies: organs, doses, routes, timing, and outcomes were too heterogeneous.
claims.source_title: BPC 157 in Rodent Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury: A Critical Review of Preclinical Evidence
claims.supporting_quote: Meta-analysis was not performed because of substantial heterogeneity in organ systems, injury paradigms, doses, routes, treatment timing, and outcome measures.

claims.claim: A chitosan hydrogel carrying BPC-157 encapsulated 98.9 percent of the peptide, released 81.2 percent within 24 hours, inhibited E. coli by 45.9 percent and S. aureus by 65.0 percent, and showed hemolysis under 5 percent.
claims.episode_span: Encapsulation was 98.9 ± 0.8 percent, with 81.2 ± 2.9 percent released within 24 hours.
claims.source_title: Fabrication and characterization of biocompatible BPC-157 based chitosan hydrogel
claims.supporting_quote: Furthermore, the hydrogel demonstrated excellent encapsulation (98.9 ± 0.8%) of BPC-157, with release profile of 81.2 ± 2.9% within 24 h.
